results.input: OpenRouter text-model routing, per-request billing, provider prompt caching, and failed/fallback attempts

output.caveats: Rates are dynamic and can vary by model, provider endpoint, model version, modality, cache state, request-scoped charges, and conditional pricing overrides such as prompt-token thresholds or UTC time windows. The GPT-4o figure is a point-in-time official API example, not a universal OpenRouter rate. Provider routing may select different endpoints; manual order/filter constraints can change availability and cache-hit behavior. Failed/fallback attempts are not documented as a separate universal fee schedule; the official fallback documentation states the ultimately used model determines request pricing, so do not assume every failed attempt is billed separately absent generation-level usage evidence.
output.observed_rates: No single universal OpenRouter rate: pricing varies by model and provider and is exposed in USD per token/request/unit. Concrete official Models API example for OpenAI GPT-4o: prompt $0.0000025/token ($2.50 per million input tokens), completion $0.00001/token ($10.00 per million output tokens), and input cache read $0.00000125/token ($1.25 per million cached input tokens); no request charge was present in the returned record. OpenRouter states it passes through underlying-provider inference pricing without markup; credit purchases are separately charged 5.5% with an $0.80 minimum via Stripe, or 5% for crypto.
output.relevant_terms: Per-request billing: models may charge fixed request fees, and image/reasoning/web-search pricing may also be listed; the Models API pricing object exposes prompt, completion, request, image, web_search, internal_reasoning, input_cache_read, and input_cache_write fields, all in USD per token/request/unit. Prompt caching is model/provider dependent: documented examples include cache reads at 0.25x (OpenAI depending on model, Grok, Moonshot, Google), 0.50x (OpenAI depending on model, Groq), and 0.10x (DeepSeek, Anthropic, Alibaba); Anthropic and Alibaba cache writes are 1.25x input price, while many automatic cache writes are free. OpenRouter uses provider-sticky routing after cache use; sticky sessions expire after 10 minutes of inactivity, and sticky routing is bypassed by manual provider.order. Provider routing is filterable/configurable with order, allow_fallbacks, require_parameters, data_collection, zdr, only, ignore, quantizations, sort, and max_price. Provider fallback is enabled by default; model fallbacks can trigger on provider/model errors including context-length validation, moderation filtering, rate limits, and downtime. Fallback model requests are priced using the model ultimately used, as returned in the response model field. Usage responses expose cost, prompt/completion tokens, cached_tokens, and cache_write_tokens for auditing.

results.input: Anthropic direct API narrator pricing and prompt-cache read/write pricing

output.caveats: Rates vary by model/version and feature; the official table includes limited-availability and retired models. The Claude API is global by default; Anthropic documents a 1.1x multiplier for inference_geo="us" on Claude 4.6 and later, and says prompt-cache multipliers stack with modifiers such as Batch API discounts and data residency. The evidence is Anthropic direct/API documentation only; Bedrock, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry, and AWS Marketplace billing can differ. Anthropic’s pricing page notes Sonnet 5’s $2/$10 rate is now standard rather than the previously scheduled September 1, 2026 increase.
output.observed_rates: Anthropic direct Claude API list prices are USD per million tokens (MTok). Active-model examples/current table: Claude Opus 5, Opus 4.8/4.7/4.6/4.5: $5 input, $25 output; Claude Sonnet 5: $2 input, $10 output; Sonnet 4.6/4.5: $3 input, $15 output; Claude Haiku 4.5: $1 input, $5 output. Prompt-cache pricing is model-specific: 5-minute writes = 1.25x base input, 1-hour writes = 2x base input, cache hits/refreshes = 0.1x base input. Thus, for the named models: Opus family = $6.25/MTok (5m write), $10/MTok (1h write), $0.50/MTok (read/refresh); Sonnet 5 = $2.50, $4, $0.20/MTok; Sonnet 4.6/4.5 = $3.75, $6, $0.30/MTok; Haiku 4.5 = $1.25, $2, $0.10/MTok. The official table also lists Fable 5 and limited-availability Mythos 5 at $10 input/$50 output, with $12.50 (5m write), $20 (1h write), and $1 (read/refresh) per MTok. Retired models remain listed with their stated rates: Opus 4.1/4 = $15 input/$75 output; Sonnet 4 = $3/$15; Haiku 3.5 = $0.80/$4, with corresponding cache rates shown in the official table.
output.relevant_terms: Default prompt-cache lifetime is 5 minutes; each use refreshes the cached prefix at no additional refresh charge. A 1-hour TTL is available at the higher 2x write rate. Minimum cacheable prompt length on the Claude API is model-dependent: 512 tokens for Opus 5/Fable 5/Mythos 5; 1,024 for Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Sonnet 4.6/4.5 and some legacy models; 4,096 for Opus 4.6/4.5 and Haiku 4.5; 2,048 for Opus 4.7 and Haiku 3.5; Mythos Preview is 2,048. Below the threshold, the request is processed without caching and no error is returned. Cached prefixes expire after at least the stated TTL/inactivity period; no manual-clear mechanism is stated. Cache pricing is filterable by model and cache event type, but the official direct API pages do not state an idle fee, minimum monetary charge, fallback fee, or content filtering surcharge.

results.input: DeepSeek direct API pricing and cache-hit/cache-miss pricing

output.caveats: Rates are model-version-specific and vary by peak/off-peak UTC time. The official release note says the new pricing took effect at 16:00 UTC on 2026-08-16. DeepSeek states that product prices may vary and reserves the right to adjust them, so the pricing page should be rechecked for future model or rate changes.
output.observed_rates: Direct DeepSeek API prices are per 1M tokens. deepseek-v4-flash (model version DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731): input cache hit $0.007/1M tokens off-peak and $0.014/1M peak; input cache miss $0.22/1M off-peak and $0.44/1M peak; output $0.66/1M off-peak and $1.32/1M peak. deepseek-v4-pro (DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813): input cache hit $0.022/1M off-peak and $0.044/1M peak; input cache miss $0.66/1M off-peak and $1.32/1M peak; output $1.98/1M off-peak and $3.96/1M peak. Billing is based on total input and output tokens, with the applicable cache-hit/cache-miss and time-of-day rate.
output.relevant_terms: Context caching is enabled by default for all users and is best-effort, with no guaranteed hit rate. Cache hits apply to fully matching persisted cache-prefix units; the API reports prompt_cache_hit_tokens and prompt_cache_miss_tokens in usage. Cache construction takes seconds, and unused cache is automatically cleared, usually within a few hours to a few days. Peak hours are 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC; all other hours are off-peak. Off-peak rates are 50% of peak. Fees are deducted from topped-up or granted balance, with granted balance used first when both are available. No idle fee, minimum bill, fallback, or user-selectable filtering term is stated.

results.input: Fireworks AI hosted serverless text inference pricing and any prompt-cache or batch terms

output.caveats: Rates and availability are model-, variant-, and serving-path-specific and may change; Fast variants and Priority have separate pricing, and Priority is unavailable for some models. The published table is the pricing source of truth for Priority availability. US-only pricing is region-specific, and EU-only Serverless is described as contact-sales rather than given a public rate. Serverless models may be updated or deprecated, with Fireworks documenting at least two weeks' advance notice before removal. Batch discount language is relative to standard Serverless rates and applies only to batch-compatible models.
output.observed_rates: Fireworks does not publish one universal hosted-serverless text rate; rates vary by model and serving path and are listed in USD per 1 million tokens. Published Standard examples: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B A3B: $0.05 input / $0.01 cached input / $0.20 output per 1M tokens; OpenAI GPT OSS 120B: $0.15 / $0.015 / $0.60 per 1M; Kimi K3: $3.00 / $0.30 / $15.00 per 1M. Other unlisted base text models are priced by size at $0.10 per 1M tokens (<4B parameters), $0.20 (4B–16B), $0.90 (>16B), or MoE tiers of $0.50 (up to 56B) and $1.20 (56.1B–176B), with the size-based rate applying uniformly to input and output. Priority prices are separately listed where available. Batch inference is billed at 50% of standard Serverless pricing for input and output; the batch guide additionally states automatic prompt caching can provide another 50% saving on cached tokens.
output.relevant_terms: Serverless bills input tokens, cached input tokens, and generated/output tokens; the response usage object is the billing source of truth. Prompt caching is enabled by default, uses exact-prefix matching, is replica-local, and cached tokens receive a model-specific discount (default 50% of input; exact discount varies by model). Stable user or session affinity via the user field or x-session-affinity can improve cache hits. Cached prompts usually remain for at least several minutes and may persist up to several hours depending on model, load, and deployment configuration; oldest entries are evicted first. Batch jobs are asynchronous, not all models are batch-compatible, and unsupported jobs may remain pending. US-only Serverless carries a 10% premium over base serverless prices, except GLM 5.2 Fast US, which matches global pricing. No idle-time or minimum-token billing is stated for Serverless; the documented basis is per token used.

results.input: RunPod GPU cloud on-demand and serverless GPU pricing for a 24 GB-class Warden deployment

output.caveats: RunPod does not publish one universal 24 GB rate: price varies by GPU model/class, product (Pods versus Serverless), and configuration. The official pricing page states that the latest Pod GPU price is shown in the RunPod console during deployment, so the listed figures are observed public examples rather than a guaranteed universal quote. Serverless groups multiple GPU types under one displayed rate, and endpoint documentation separately lists 4090 PRO; fallback selection can change the actual GPU used and rate. Availability depends on host capacity and data-center restrictions; restricting data centers reduces the available pool. Evidence is official RunPod material accessed 2026-08-18.
output.observed_rates: Pods on-demand Community Cloud published examples for 24 GB-class GPUs: RTX A5000 $0.27/GPU-hour; L4 $0.49/GPU-hour; RTX 3090 $0.50/GPU-hour; RTX 4090 $0.74/GPU-hour. Serverless published examples: 24 GB L4/A5000/3090/MIG 24GB $0.69/GPU-hour, equivalent to $0.00019/GPU-second; 24 GB 4090 $1.10/GPU-hour, with endpoint documentation listing 4090 PRO at $0.00031/GPU-second (approximately $1.116/GPU-hour). Pods are billed per second despite rates being displayed per hour; Serverless is billed per second, rounded up to the nearest second, from worker start until it fully stops.
output.relevant_terms: Pods on-demand has no commitment and requires at least one hour of credits for the selected configuration before deployment. Serverless flex workers scale to zero and cost nothing while idle/not running; active workers run continuously and incur charges even when idle, with discounts available through sales inquiry. Serverless billing includes initialization/start time, execution time, and idle-timeout duration; default idle timeout is 5 seconds and is billed. Endpoint GPU selection supports up to three prioritized GPU types as fallback; with fewer than five workers, all workers use the highest-priority available type. Serverless initializing, idle (scaled down), throttled, and unhealthy states are not billed; running state is billed. Storage and account-balance terms are additional to GPU compute.

results.input: Lambda Cloud GPU cloud on-demand pricing for a 24 GB-class or 48 GB-class deployment

output.caveats: Rates are dynamic and availability/price depend on the instance type and geographical region; Lambda’s on-demand documentation says the listed instance catalog was current as of December 2025, while the live pricing page accessed 2026-08-18 omitted the 24 GB and 48 GB rows. Therefore no auditable current universal 24 GB/48 GB public rate can be asserted from unauthenticated official pages. The API may provide current per-instance pricing after authentication. Historical Lambda blog pricing such as $0.60/hour for an A10 is not treated as current evidence.
output.observed_rates: No current public list price was displayed for the 24 GB A10/RTX 6000 or 48 GB A6000 classes on Lambda’s official pricing page accessed 2026-08-18. The page currently publishes adjacent on-demand examples of $1.99/GPU/hour for NVIDIA A100 SXM 40 GB, $2.79/GPU/hour for A100 SXM 80 GB, $3.99/GPU/hour for H100 SXM 80 GB, $6.69/GPU/hour for B200 SXM6 180 GB, and $0.79/GPU/hour for Tesla V100 16 GB. Lambda’s official API documentation states that the authenticated “List available instance types” endpoint returns current instance specifications, pricing, and regional availability, but the public documentation does not expose a universal 24 GB/48 GB rate without an API key.
output.relevant_terms: On-Demand Cloud instances are priced by hourly usage and billed in one-minute increments. Billing begins when the instance launches and passes health checks and ends when it is terminated; billing continues while running even if actively unused. The pricing-page footnote says listed prices are plus applicable sales tax/VAT/GST. No cache, idle-time waiver, minimum-billing period, discount, fallback, or public filterability terms were stated for the requested 24 GB/48 GB classes.

results.input: Vast.ai marketplace GPU on-demand price mechanics and concrete 24 GB-class hourly examples

output.caveats: Rates are dynamic marketplace prices set by hosts and supply/demand across data centers; the official GPU pages state that displayed prices reflect currently available offers and update hourly. Actual cost varies by offer, host, region, reliability, instance type, storage allocation, and bandwidth usage. The 24 GB examples are concrete observations, not guaranteed rates or forecasts; interruptible and reserved pricing are different classes and should not be mixed with on-demand.
output.observed_rates: Official live pricing evidence accessed 2026-08-18 showed RTX 3090 (24 GB) at $0.07 per GPU-hour and RTX 4090 (24 GB GDDR6X) at $0.13 per GPU-hour. These are marketplace offer rates, not universal fixed list prices; active on-demand rental is billed per second, so the hourly figure is the rate basis rather than a one-hour minimum.
output.relevant_terms: Vast.ai states on-demand instances have guaranteed uptime, no interruptions, per-second billing, and no minimum hours or rounding up. Active GPU rental is charged for each second in the active/connected state. Storage is charged per second while an instance exists online, including when stopped, and bandwidth is charged per byte transferred; offline instances incur neither active-rental nor storage charges. The official search-offers API supports filtering/querying offers, including on-demand type, GPU characteristics such as total GPU RAM, and hourly-price fields such as total_hourly/discounted_hourly and dph_total.

results.input: Black Forest Labs direct FLUX API image pricing and safety/moderation terms

output.caveats: There is no single universal image rate: current pricing varies by model, operation, output resolution/megapixels, and preview or fixed-snapshot endpoint; FLUX.2 prices are explicitly 'from' rates and the official calculator is recommended for exact cost. FLUX.2 [dev] is listed as local-only with no hosted API. Enterprise/large-volume pricing is custom and may include volume discounts. The evidence reflects official pages accessed on 2026-08-18; the pricing overview identifies FLUX.1 as previous generation.
output.observed_rates: Official pricing is credit-based: 1 credit = $0.01 USD; API and Playground use the same prices. Current listed image rates include FLUX.2 [klein] 4B from $0.014 per output image/first megapixel, 9B from $0.015 per image/first megapixel, [pro] from $0.03 per image/first megapixel for text-to-image and from $0.045 for image editing, [max] from $0.07, and [flex] from $0.05; FLUX.1 Kontext [pro] $0.04/image, Kontext [max] $0.08/image, FLUX1.1 [pro] $0.04/image, FLUX1.1 [pro] Ultra $0.06/image, FLUX1.1 [pro] Raw $0.06/image, and FLUX.1 Fill [pro] $0.05/image. FLUX.2 rates are resolution-dependent: after the first MP, each additional MP adds to the total; e.g., a 2MP Klein 4B image is $0.015. Batch requests multiply the base cost by image count (e.g., four FLUX.2 [pro] images from $0.12).
output.relevant_terms: Pay-as-you-go credits; no subscription or seat-fee pricing is stated on the official pricing page. No cache discount, idle fee, minimum billing increment, or fallback charge is stated. API result schema exposes settled request cost in credits. Moderation is operationally visible: API statuses include Request Moderated and Content Moderated; model parameters expose safety_tolerance from 0 (most strict) to 6 (more permissive), default 2. Terms allow BFL to restrict, remove, prevent, or disable content/functionality/access for Usage Policy or legal violations. Usage Policy prohibits unlawful content, non-consensual intimate imagery, certain deceptive/impersonation/harassing content, military/surveillance/law-enforcement and biometric/high-risk uses, and IP-infringing content. API limits are 24 active tasks (6 for flux-kontext-max); signed result URLs expire after 10 minutes.

results.input: Replicate FLUX image-model pricing and relevant moderation/filter capabilities

output.caveats: Rates vary materially by model generation/version and billing unit: older FLUX.1 models are per output image, while FLUX.2 models may charge per run and/or input/output megapixel. The pricing page is dynamic and model pages are the authoritative source for the selected version. Input-image megapixel charges apply only where the model’s published basis includes them. Safety behavior and configurability can differ by model/version and deployment path; Replicate’s general safety page explicitly covers Flux base and derivative fine-tunes, not necessarily every future FLUX endpoint. Evidence is official Replicate material only; no third-party pricing was used.
output.observed_rates: Replicate’s official public pricing is model-specific rather than one universal FLUX rate. Published examples observed: FLUX1.1 [pro] $0.04 per output image; FLUX.1 [dev] $0.025 per output image; FLUX.1 [schnell] $3.00 per 1,000 output images ($0.003/image). Current FLUX.2 examples: FLUX.2 [pro] $0.015 per run, plus $0.015 per input image megapixel and $0.015 per output image megapixel; FLUX.2 [max] $0.04 per run, plus $0.03 per input image megapixel and $0.03 per output image megapixel; FLUX.2 [flex] $0.06 per input image megapixel and $0.06 per output image megapixel. Replicate states some models are billed by hardware/time and others by input/output, so use the exact model page’s pricing basis.
output.relevant_terms: Replicate is pay-as-you-go. The cited FLUX official-model pages describe predictable pricing and official models as always on; no cache discount, idle surcharge, minimum per-prediction charge, or fallback price was stated for these FLUX list prices. Replicate’s safety documentation states that Black Forest Labs’ Flux base model and derivative fine-tunes include a safety checker intended to prevent nudity, violence, and other unsafe content. For API predictions, Replicate says users have flexibility to use a custom safety-checking model or a third-party service as part of the workflow; the cited documentation does not promise a universal disable switch for every FLUX version. Billing documentation distinguishes public model pricing from private dedicated models, where idle online time can be billed; that private-model rule should not be applied to these official FLUX list prices without verification.

results.input: fal.ai FLUX image-model pricing and relevant moderation/filter capabilities

output.caveats: There is no single universal FLUX rate: pricing varies by model/version and, for FLUX.2 [pro], by megapixel accounting for input and output. Rates and schemas are model-page-specific and may change; this record reflects the official pages accessed on 2026-08-18. No cache, idle, or fallback discount terms were stated on the reviewed official pages. results.input: ComfyUI local deployment licensing/cost-relevant documentation and safety/filter-control implications

output.caveats: No single universal USD on-demand rate exists for local deployment: ComfyUI software is open-source, while total operating cost depends on user-owned hardware and selected models/nodes. Desktop licensing is dual-license, so commercial redistribution or deployment should be assessed against AGPL terms or a commercial Comfy Org license. Cloud prices and credits are a hosted-service reference only, vary by plan and annual/monthly billing, and the pricing page's example output is workflow/model/parameter dependent. Enterprise pricing is undisclosed. Model and custom-node licenses, provider terms, and safety filters are separate from the ComfyUI core license.
output.observed_rates: Local ComfyUI core has no published software license fee: the official repository is GPL-3.0, and the official documentation states Comfy Desktop is dual-licensed under AGPL-3.0-or-later or a commercial Comfy Org license. Local hardware, electricity, storage, GPU, and model licensing costs are not stated by ComfyUI. As a concrete official hosted benchmark, Comfy Cloud lists Standard at $20/month monthly or $16/month equivalent when billed yearly ($192/year), Creator at $35/month monthly or $28/month equivalent yearly ($336/year), Pro at $100/month monthly or $80/month equivalent yearly ($960/year), and Team at $700/month ($7,560/year); these are credit-pool subscriptions, not local-deployment rates. Enterprise local-instance licensing has no public dollar rate and is contact-sales/custom pricing.
output.relevant_terms: Local ComfyUI runs fully offline; the official repository says core does not download anything unless requested, and --disable-api-nodes disables optional paid API nodes to keep built-in functionality offline. Comfy Cloud charges only active GPU time; idle workflow-building/editing time is free, each run has a 30-minute maximum (1 hour on Pro), and over-limit jobs are automatically cancelled. Cloud monthly credits reset and do not roll over; purchased top-ups remain valid for 1 year. Partner Nodes consume credits according to model and parameters; BYOK calls for supported providers are billed directly by that provider rather than Comfy credits. The official Ideogram workflow documentation identifies image blocking as Ideogram 4.0's built-in safety filter. No universal ComfyUI-local content filter or mandatory platform-wide safety filter is stated; local model/node/provider behavior governs filtering, while optional Partner/API nodes may apply provider-specific controls.
